text: the fruit by which persons are designated as stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, arhat, pratyekabuddha, and Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha — are those dharmas that establish persons also emanations?" The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, all dharmas are emanations. Among them, some are emanations of śrāvakas, some are emanations of pratyekabuddhas, some are emanations of bodhisattvas, some are emanations of Tathāgatas, some are emanations of the afflictions, some are emanations of karma. Subhūti, in this sense all dharmas are emanations." He said, "Blessed One, what is called abandonment — the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or non-returning itself, or the level of a pratyekabuddha, or the level of a buddha, the abandonment of all the connections of latent tendencies — are all those dharmas also emanations?" The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, whatever dharma is produced or stopped, all of it is emanation." He said, "Blessed One, what is the dharma that is not an emanation?" The Blessed One said, "The dharma in which there is neither arising nor ceasing is not an emanation." He said, "What is that?" The Blessed One said, "Unequalled nirvāṇa; that dharma is not an emanation." [unclear]
